subtype: Approach: accepting a real limit and deferring the desire [Revision]
passage: Every option had been tried. The camp ran the same two weeks as the winter stock rush, Cousin Ravi was away, and the shorter programme in the city was full. Lalit sat with his father Vikas at the counter after closing, pushing a pencil back and forth. “So we can't,” Lalit said. “Not this year.” Vikas nodded, and a heavy quiet filled the shop. Then Lalit pulled over a fresh sheet and wrote a heading: NEXT YEAR. Under it he wrote: apply the day registration opens in January; ask Mr Nair for a recommendation letter; ask Papa to plan the shop cover for that fortnight early. “It's late, not lost,” he said. Vikas read the list twice. “Put my name next to the third one,” he said.

qa.q: When will Lalit apply next year?
qa.a: The day registration opens in January.

qa.q: How does Lalit feel about skipping this year, and how can you tell?
qa.a: Disappointed but steady: he pushes the pencil around in silence, then writes a plan and calls the camp late, not lost.

qa.q: What else could Lalit do to keep the goal alive this year, and why?
qa.a: He could build a small robot project at home or join a free online club, since practice through the year keeps his skills growing until the next camp.

qa.q: How does the plan look to Vikas?
qa.a: Vikas sees his son accept a hard limit without blaming anyone, and the list gives him a concrete part to play, so it becomes a shared goal.

grounding: When no option works this year, a student skips the camp but writes a plan to apply next year with parental support.
